title: Customer-managed connectivity minimalism — PRD brain dump
body:
Context / motivation:
This is a working PRD sketch for a lightweight approval and audit footprint mode aimed at customers who want to manage their own VPC/edge connectivity but are sensitive to telemetry volume, retention costs, and operator overhead. The core idea: provide a Minimal Change Path (MCP) API + UX that records just enough verifiable evidence to support post-hoc investigation and compliance, while letting customers keep most traffic/telemetry inside their network.

Problems we hear from customers:
- "We can't ship huge audit logs off-network due to cost and policy."
- "Every small firewall tweak triggers full evidence collection and creates noise for our SOC."
- "We need a lightweight handoff that the vendor can rely on if something goes wrong, but we don't want all our network flows mirrored."

Goals (what success looks like):
- Define an MCP contract that reduces evidence payloads by ~80% vs full capture while preserving reconstructability for common incident classes.
- Expose an approval API that takes <100ms extra latency on onboarding flows and supports automated integration with customer ticketing/SOA.
- Offer operator UX and heuristics for when to escalate to full evidence capture (e.g., anomalous drift, failed rollbacks).
- Provide clear cost/retention tradeoffs and safe defaults for compliance-sensitive customers.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full-forensic mode (we still keep an opt-in full-capture).
- Not intended to bypass regulatory retention minima; customers still responsible for jurisdictional requirements.

High-level design (sketch):
1) Minimal Change Path (MCP) evidence envelope
   - CompactApproval object (signed): { actor-id, change-hash, manifest-summary, timestamp, approval-level, short-excerpt-of-diff }
   - SnapshotHint (optional): tiny digest pointers to locally-stored PCAP/Config bundles with retention pointers (customer-managed URLs or hashed pointers).
   - Immutable receipt: Redwoodsigned(assertion-id, change-hash, TTL) to show we observed the handshake.
   - Keep full artifacts local to customer by default; Redwood stores only the compact envelope and receipt.

2) Approval gates and UX
   - Fast-path approvals: when change matches low-risk policy (whitelisted CIDR, operator tag), generate MCP envelope automatically.
   - Canary/rollback meta: approval response includes recommended observation window and rollback-safety-checks (lightweight).
   - Operator flow: single-click escalate -> full evidence capture for the next N minutes (configurable).

3) APIs (minimal examples)
   - POST /mcp/prepare-change -> returns change-id, suggested-evidence-level, signed-preflight-token
   - POST /mcp/commit-change -> body: { change-id, signed-approval, optional snapshot-hints } -> returns immutable-receipt
   - GET /mcp/receipt/{id} -> returns compact envelope (signed), meta: retention-window, escalation-links

4) Audit and reconstruction guarantees
   - MCP should provide deterministic mapping from compact envelope + snapshot-hints to a reconstructable timeline for: config changes, observed endpoint connectivity changes, approval chain.
   - Define minimal retention window for compact envelopes (default 365d) and separate SLA/contract for customer-managed artifacts.
Acceptance criteria (draft):
- MCP API implemented with test harness that simulates 10k small changes/day and verifies storing compact envelopes consumes <20% storage vs full logs.
- UX flows in the Console for escalate/rollback visible from the change card within 2 clicks.
- Integration tests with customer-managed S3-like endpoints for snapshot-hints using signed URLs and TTLs.
- Security review: signatures use customer KMS or Redwood HSM depending on deployment mode; threat model review passed.

Edge cases and escalation heuristics (notes):
- If a change fails to converge or triggers policy anomalies, automatically switch to temporary full-capture with a 24h audit TTL.
- If customer denies sharing artifacts during an investigation, evidence envelope still provides traceable assertion chain (who approved, when, manifest-summary) to support first-pass triage.

Operational considerations:
- Storage: compact envelopes indexed by change-hash, tenant-id, approver-id. Keep lightweight search indices for fast lookup.
- Cost: add MCP as a lower-cost storage tier; default retention shorter but configurable by customers.
- Privacy: do not ingest or persist full network payloads unless explicitly escalated.

Rollout plan (rough):
- Phase 0: internal prototype + sim harness (2 sprint) -> validate compression ratio and signature plumbing.
- Phase 1: beta with 2 customers (security-first & low-bandwidth) to validate UX and SLA semantics (6 weeks).
- Phase 2: GA with Console controls, default presets, and docs (Q3).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Signature model across Private deployments: prefer customer KMS or Redwood HSM? hybrid approach? (action: security deep-dive).
- What is the canonical manifest-summary format? JSON lines? proto? (action: decide by API review).
- Retention defaults per region / regulatory constraints (action: compliance consult).
- How to surface MCP receipts into customer SIEMs without leaking payloads (webhooks vs pull)?

Notes / UX snippets (brain dump):
- Console change card: shows small badge "MCP" when compact evidence recorded, with hover: "Minimal Change Path — compact evidence retained. Click to view receipt or escalate."
- Quick-rollback CTA: "Revert and capture full evidence for 30m" (operator permission gated).
- Example Slack alert payload (short): { change-id, tenant, approver, risk-score, receipt-link }

Risks:
- Customers assuming MCP replaces legal retention obligations -> mitigation: explicit contract language and console nudges.
- Under-collection leads to blind spots in rare incidents -> mitigation: conservative defaults + automatic escalation heuristics.

Next steps (immediate):
- Align with Security and Compliance on signature/KMS model (owner: Aisha).
- Create JIRA epic (PRIV-4123) with sub-tasks for API, console, sim harness (owner: Marco).
- Propose API proto sketch in GH PR (owner: Riley) -> link above.

Appendix (links & references):
- Similar concept: internal "compact-evidence" experiment (archived notes in Confluence).
- Customer feedback snippets from Security pilot (anonymized) attached in linked Confluence page.

-- end of brain dump --

This is intentionally informal: want to capture options and edge cases before turning into a more formal PRD. Comments welcome — tag me in the doc or Slack #private-deployments.
